functionalObligations.text: USDT is a transferable receipt for an unsecured, on-demand claim against a single private company, Tether International, S.A. de C.V., incorporated in El Salvador and authorised by the Comision Nacional de Activos Digitales under DASP registration PSAD-0028; the attested accounts classify the outstanding tokens as a refund liability under IFRS 9.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the category headline. There is no symbol for 'an El Salvadoran S.A. de C.V. owes you', none for the obligor at all, and none for creditor priority against it. The single most decision-relevant fact about USDT -- that the instrument is an unsecured refund liability of a private company -- is stated in the auditor's own classification and has no name in the 58. CORPUS CORRECTION: the corpus records the obligor as 'Tether Limited'; the customer-facing issuer at the 2026-02-20 RID is Tether International, S.A. de C.V., and the BDO opinion is addressed to that entity and no other.

functionalObligations.text: The claim is to face value only: holders are not entitled to any increase in the value of the reserves in excess of the face value of the tokens, so the reserve surplus of US$4,109,529,196 at 2026-06-30 belongs to the shareholder and the holder is senior at par with no upside.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Tr (tranche waterfall) was considered and REJECTED, and the reason is worth stage 4's attention: this is a declared seniority over a loss event -- a one-line waterfall with holders at par and the shareholder taking the residual -- and law L6's own terms for Tr (declared seniority, dispute forum, recovery-timing assumption) are all satisfiable off-chain. USDT supplies two of the three (seniority; BVI-law arbitration seated in London). Tr is withheld only because no mechanism executes the waterfall: it is a sentence in a PDF and an insolvency outcome. The vocabulary offers no way to distinguish a declared seniority from an enforced one.

functionalObligations.text: The right to present the claim is not a property of holding the token: only 819 KYC Verified Customers may redeem, as of 2026-02-16, against a holder base of hundreds of millions; everyone else holds a bearer instrument whose only exit is the secondary market.
functionalObligations.note: BOTH APPROXIMATE. Rd asserts a 'direct redemption right' and is silent on who holds it; here it is held by 819 named counterparties and by nobody else, so the symbol is true of the system and false of essentially every holder -- the same defect the bridges lane recorded for WBTC's 47 merchants. Aw is a CORPUS DEPARTURE: the corpus assigns Aw to USDC alone, on the reasoning that 'the gate is on Circle Mint access'. Tether's gate is identical in kind (KYC Verified Customer status, sole issuer discretion to reject) and was not coded. Either all five carry Aw or none does; this lane carries it in all five and marks it approximate wherever the gate is an off-chain business relationship rather than an on-chain check. Law L16 (Aw -> transfer-time enforcement where eligibility follows the holder) is NOT satisfied: USDT transfers are permissionless.

functionalObligations.text: Redemption carries a minimum of US$100,000 and a fee of the greater of US$1,000 or 0.1%, settles by fiat wire to the customer's bank account, and has no published settlement-time commitment -- the lifecycle is six steps with no service level.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE. Rd carries no minimum, no fee and no latency, and those three parameters are what actually decide whether the peg holds under stress. Redemption latency is UNKNOWN as a contractual matter -- the issuer commits to no bound. Wq (withdrawal queue) was considered and rejected: there is no queue, on-chain or stated; there is an unbounded discretionary process.

functionalObligations.text: The issuer may delay or suspend redemption where it determines a Prohibited Use, where directed by any government, where the account is under investigation, or on suspicion of fraud, and maintains sole discretion to approve or reject applications to become a customer at all.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Sv (servicing & determination discretion, candidate) was considered and REJECTED: Sv names a servicer's discretion over the performance status of an instrument whose determination feeds a state transition the model can see. Here the discretion is the obligor's own, over its own performance, exercised off-chain, unobservable and unfalsifiable. Flagged for stage 4 as the nearest existing candidate if 'obligor discretion to refuse performance' is to be given a home -- it would require broadening Sv from servicer to obligor.

functionalObligations.text: The reserve at 2026-06-30 is US$187,751,426,411 of total assets against US$183,641,897,215 of liabilities, of which US$183,622,105,630 is digital tokens issued: US$114.96bn of Treasury bills under 90 days, US$25.62bn of repo, US$18.84bn of LBMA gold bars, US$5.80bn of bitcoin, US$3.76bn of public equities, US$5.24bn of other investments and US$13.45bn of secured loans.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, confirmed against the corpus's own residue list and sharper than it. Nothing in the 58 distinguishes US$114.96bn of sub-90-day T-bills from US$18.84bn of gold bars from US$13.45bn of over-collateralised secured loans, and that difference is the entire instrument. At names the PDF that describes the reserve; there is no symbol for the reserve. This is the strongest single instance in the project of the claim that everything determining whether the token is worth a dollar sits outside the model.

functionalObligations.text: Cash and bank deposits are US$40,307,440, which is 0.02% of the reserve, and roughly US$23.6bn (12.6%) is gold, bitcoin, equities, other investments and secured loans -- assets whose realisable value in a redemption run is a judgement.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Prohibition X5 ('illiquid backing + uncapped instant par redemption') and law L14 ('illiquid backing -> Wq | bounded liquidity reserve') both quantify over a predicate -- 'illiquid backing' -- that no element of the vocabulary can evaluate, because the backing is not in the model. The corpus records armedProhibitions: [] for USDT; the honest statement is not that X5 is unarmed but that it is UNDECIDABLE in this carrier. That is a finding about the tables, not about Tether.

functionalObligations.text: No bank, depositary or custodian is named anywhere in the primary record: the offering document says only that the issuer 'primarily holds the Reserves with various third parties including banks and licensed financial institutions', and the assurance report names none.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and now unobservable as well as unnameable. The corpus lists banking and correspondent relationships as residue because the historical failure mode was a banking failure; at 2026-08-04 the primary documents do not name a single counterparty, so the fact is not merely unrepresentable in the model, it is unavailable to any modeller. Named banking and custody relationships: UNKNOWN from primary sources.

functionalObligations.text: Assurance is quarterly and is an ISAE 3000 (Revised) reasonable-assurance engagement by BDO Advisory Services S.r.l., Milan, partner Lelio Bigogno, dated 2026-07-31, on the Financial Figures and Reserves Report as of 2026-06-30 23:59 UTC, with procedures including bank and depositary confirmation letters, third-party inventory and assay testing of precious metals on a sample basis, blockchain-to-ledger reconciliation and collateral verification on a sample of secured loans.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE. Against law L27 (At -> named attester + independence + stated assurance + staleness bound + recourse) this satisfies three of five: named attester yes, independence yes, stated assurance level yes and at the highest available (reasonable assurance is the assurance level of an audit opinion). Staleness bound: no -- the cadence is quarterly by practice, not by covenant, and the report is point-in-time. Recourse: none. CORPUS CORRECTION: the corpus flags 'attestation vs audit' as the interesting distinction; it is not. The engagement is reasonable assurance. The interesting gap is F10.

functionalObligations.text: The attester expressly declines the solvency judgement: no assurance is given on the going-concern assessment, the Notes are outside the engagement, and the valuations 'do not reflect unexpected and extraordinary market conditions, or the case of key custodians or counterparties experiencing substantial illiquidity'.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a first-class one. At has no place to record what the attester REFUSED to say. Reasonable assurance on a schedule of assets says nothing about whether the entity can pay, and the auditor says so in terms. A model that carries At and not its carve-outs records the strongest possible signal about the reserve while discarding the explicit statement that the signal does not cover the question the reader is asking.

functionalObligations.text: The regulator is El Salvador's CNAD; disputes are routed to confidential BVI-law arbitration seated in London before a sole arbitrator; there is no deposit insurance, no trust, no stated security interest and no segregation covenant.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. No symbol for a supervising authority, for what it may order, or for a dispute forum. Compare USDG, whose white paper names the District Court of Helsinki: 'who do you sue' is answerable for three of the five and unrepresentable for all five.

functionalObligations.text: On-chain the token is plain balance accounting: TetherToken at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, Solidity 0.4.18, 6 decimals, Ethereum supply 92,056,579,574.486405 at 2026-08-04, inheriting Pausable, StandardToken and BlackList from a single Ownable with no role separation whatsoever.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call totalSupply(), paused(), owner() at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE of a kind the corpus does not record at all. The claims-and-accounting group offers Sh (pro-rata pool share), Ix (index accrual) and Rb (rebasing); a fixed-unit transferable balance is none of the three, and it is what every member of this category actually is. The vocabulary can name three ways a claim's value can move and has no name for a claim whose value does not move.

functionalObligations.text: Issuance and destruction are treasury operations, not user-facing: issue(uint) and redeem(uint) are onlyOwner and mint to and burn from the owner's own balance; no contract function observes, values or is constrained by the reserve, and the contract contains no reference to a reserve.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a CORPUS DEPARTURE. Ps (peg-swap module, 1:1 reserve-backed) is DROPPED from this construction. The corpus carried Ps and marked it forced; carrying it imputes an on-chain 1:1 reserve mechanism that does not exist -- there is no module, no reserve object, no swap and no counter-asset. The bridges lane rejected Ps on identical reasoning for WBTC ('no on-chain module holding a reserve to swap 1:1 against'); this lane applies the same test and drops Ps from ALL FIVE members of the category. Under the project's standing rule that a finding of failure beats a forced fit, the honest record is that the category's defining behaviour -- one token, one dollar -- is discharged by no element.

functionalObligations.text: The issuer can freeze and irreversibly destroy any balance: addBlackList(address), removeBlackList(address) and destroyBlackFunds(address) are onlyOwner, the last emitting DestroyedBlackFunds; there is no forced transfer, only destruction.
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE REGISTER, used with a note as the contract requires. Fz is 'freeze / forced transfer' and collapses three distinct powers with three distinct consequences for a holder: freeze (your balance is immobilised and still yours), seize-and-destroy (your balance ceases to exist), and forced transfer (your balance moves to an address chosen by someone else). USDT has freeze and destroy and NOT forced transfer; USD1 has all three; PYUSD has freeze and destroy; USDC has freeze with a three-state liability. Fz is true of all four and separates none of them.

functionalObligations.text: The trigger for freezing is a law-enforcement, regulatory or government request, and the issuer reserves the right to freeze tokens in external wallets for which it does not hold private keys; the issuer claims cooperation with more than 340 agencies in 65 countries and more than US$4.4bn frozen since launch, including more than US$344M across two addresses in coordination with OFAC on 2026-04-23.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Law L28 requires of Fz a named authority, enumerated triggers, an appeal path and holder disclosure. USDT satisfies NONE of the four in a machine-checkable way: the authority is 'any government', the triggers are open-ended, there is no appeal path and no disclosure obligation. These are issuer claims and are not independently attested; a machine-counted total of blacklisted addresses is UNKNOWN (a full eth_getLogs sweep of AddedBlackList was rate-limited off public RPC in stage 1). The corpus's own marker cites '2,000+ blacklisted addresses'; that figure is not reproducible from a primary source and this construction does not carry it.

functionalObligations.text: The issuer can halt every transfer globally: pause() and unpause() are onlyOwner; paused() reads false at 2026-08-04.
functionalObligations.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Gp is ADDED. The corpus assigns Gp to USDC alone. pause() and unpause() are present in the verified ABI of all five deployed tokens and live under a named authority in every one; verified for this contract by reading the Blockscout ABI on 2026-08-04, which lists pause and unpause. This single correction breaks the corpus's claimed identity USDT = USD1 with USDC's set and changes four of the five decompositions. It is a coding artefact, not a design difference.

functionalObligations.text: The owner can impose a fee on every transfer of the instrument: setParams(uint newBasisPoints, uint newMaxFee) sets a per-transfer basis-point rate capped by maximumFee; both read zero at 2026-08-04.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, new -- not in the corpus. Fd (surplus & fee distribution) was considered and REJECTED: this is a levy on holders with no distribution rule attached, not a distribution of surplus. The deeper gap is that no symbol names a LATENT mechanism. The vocabulary is a vocabulary of what is, not of what is armed, and the distinction between 'absent' and 'set to zero by a 3-of-6 key that can change it in one transaction' is the whole risk on a US$92bn Ethereum-side float. The same gap recurs at USD1 (a null but installable compliance checker) and at USDG (capabilities that exist only while a facet table maps their selectors).

functionalObligations.text: The upgrade path is a forwarding deprecation rather than a proxy: deprecate(address _upgradedAddress) sets deprecated = true and forwards transfer, transferFrom, balanceOf, approve and allowance to a new contract implementing UpgradedStandardToken, leaving storage behind; deprecated() reads false at 2026-08-04.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE. Up is 'mutable implementation proxy'; this is not a proxy. Only five entry points forward, storage stays in the old contract, and the failure surface is different in kind -- partial forwarding and stale views rather than wholesale replacement. Up cannot distinguish a transparent proxy (USDC, PYUSD), an EIP-1967 proxy with a separate ProxyAdmin (USD1), a UUPS proxy with a facet router under it (USDG) and a five-function forwarding deprecation (USDT), and those are four different things to hold.

functionalObligations.text: Mint, burn, freeze, destroy, pause, the transfer-fee dial and the upgrade are all onlyOwner and owner() is one address, 0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828, a MultiSigWallet with 6 owners and required() == 3, with no timelock of any kind.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7 (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call owner() at 0xdAC17F958D2ee523a2206206994597C13D831ec7, getOwners() and required() at 0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828 (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the bridges lane's finding exhibited again on a larger instrument. Every control element in the vocabulary names a FACILITY -- Tg a delay, Up a proxy, Gp a pause -- and none names WHO HOLDS IT OR HOW MANY OF THEM THERE ARE. Here seven distinct powers are one 3-of-6 key. Tg is correctly absent (there is no delay) and its absence is indistinguishable from not having looked. Prohibition X9 ('Up with immediate single-key control') does NOT fire on a 3-of-6, which means the tables treat a three-signature immediate upgrade of a US$92bn instrument as unremarkable; the axis that matters is quorum against single key, and the carrier has no party sort in which to state it.

functionalObligations.text: Supply moves between Ethereum, Tron, Solana, Avalanche, TON and other chains by the issuer burning on one and issuing on another under off-chain authorisation, over a chain set determined by the issuer alone; there is no bridge contract, no message and no verifier in this path.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Xf and Xm are explicitly NOT assigned and must not be: there is no lock, no proof, no verifier set, no threshold and no message -- an employee burns here and issues there. This is the same negative finding the bridges lane recorded for the custodial wrappers, and it is the correct reading of the corpus's own residue line. It also isolates the real cross-domain difference in this category: USDC (CCTP) and USD1 (Chainlink CCIP) run verified burn-and-mint; USDT runs operator fiat; USDG and PYUSD are UNKNOWN.

functionalObligations.text: The issuer's answer to United States regulation was to create a different token with a different obligor: USAT, launched 2026-01-27, issued by Anchorage Digital Bank under OCC supervision with Cantor Fitzgerald as reserve custodian under the GENIUS Act, with separate reserves, separate issuance and separate redemption rails from USDT.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. No relation between two issuances by one corporate group is expressible in the carrier -- the same containment gap the intents and yield lanes found between protocols, here between instruments of a single issuer. It matters because the regulatory regime a token may legally exist under is chosen by picking which token to hold, and the model cannot state that two tokens are siblings, let alone that one is the compliant sibling of the other.

functionalObligations.text: There is no canonical public source repository: the authority for USDT-on-Ethereum is the verified bytecode, verified on Blockscout on 2019-04-18 as a partial (metadata-hash) match with no license declared, and the only GitHub artefact is an unofficial three-commit mirror that itself points back to a block explorer.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. No element names the correspondence, or its absence, between published source and deployed bytecode. The spot-exchange lane found the converse failure -- two artefacts sharing a version string and implementing different mathematics -- and the two together say the same thing: the model identifies a protocol by its element set and has no way to identify the artefact the element set was read from.
